title: Covenant
blurb: Trace God's covenant promises from Noah through Abraham, Sinai and David to the new covenant sealed at the Last Supper.

steps.title: A Bow in the Clouds
steps.intro: After the flood, God makes a covenant with Noah, with his descendants and with every living creature, promising never again to destroy the earth by flood. The rainbow is given as the sign of that promise.

quote.text: He offered sacrifice and stayed the flood; he presented gifts and received the promise. With prayer and incense he propitiated Thee: with an oath and with the bow Thou wast gracious to him; so that if the flood should essay to hurt the earth, the bow should stretch itself over against it, to banish it away and hearten the earth.

steps.question: What does it mean to you that God's first covenant includes all creation and not only humans?

steps.title: Stars Beyond Counting
steps.intro: Abraham, childless, is promised an heir and descendants as many as the stars. Scripture says he believed, and it was credited to him as righteousness. God then seals the promise in a covenant ritual.

quote.text: Immediately he was promised an heir, not that house-born servant, but one who was to come forth of Abraham himself; and again a seed innumerable, not as the dust of the earth, but as the stars of heaven,—which rather seems to me a promise of a posterity exalted in celestial felicity.

steps.question: Which promise of God are you finding hard to trust right now, and what would trusting it look like?

steps.title: At the Mountain
steps.intro: At Sinai, God offers Israel a covenant: obey his voice and be his treasured possession, a kingdom of priests. The people agree, and Moses seals the agreement with sacrifice and the sprinkling of blood.

quote.text: How then was that law given in time past, and when, and where? After the destruction of the Egyptians, in the wilderness, on Mount Sinai, when smoke and fire were rising up out of the mountain, a trumpet sounding, thunders and lightnings, and Moses entering into the very depth of the cloud.

steps.question: How do you understand the relationship between God's gift of freedom in Exodus and the law that follows?

steps.title: A House for David
steps.intro: Through the prophet Nathan, God promises David a lasting house, an heir whose kingdom will be established forever. Later Israel looked to this promise, and the New Testament connects it with Jesus.

quote.text: What covenant, but the new, by which we are renewed to a fresh inheritance, in our longing desire and love of which we sing a new song.

steps.question: What hope does the promise of an everlasting kingdom give you in the face of leaders who fail?

steps.title: Written on the Heart
steps.intro: Jeremiah foresees a new covenant, different from the one made at Sinai. God will place the law within his people, write it on their hearts, and forgive their sin. The Letter to the Hebrews quotes this passage at length.

quote.text: That is, besides the covenant being in itself a new one, different from the Mosaic, there is also, he says, the difference in the mode of giving it, the one being written, the other put into the heart.

steps.question: What would it look like for God's commands to be less a rulebook for you and more a desire?

steps.title: The Cup of the New Covenant
steps.intro: At the Last Supper, Jesus takes the cup and calls it the new covenant in his blood, given for his disciples. He ties the old promises to his coming death and gives a meal to be repeated.

quote.text: Since then instead of the blood of beasts He brought in His own Blood; lest any should be troubled on hearing this, He reminds them of that ancient sacrifice.

steps.question: How does remembering that the Eucharist is a covenant meal shape the way you approach Mass?
